content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge marks Matthew 1:16 UNDERDETERMINED because it admits two readings, the two-sense situation K-S2 says is not open.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand -- reading one: admitting two readings makes the link UNDERDETERMINED; reading two: the rule forbids treating that dual sense as open and requires both senses to stand.","why":"By treating the verse's two admitted readings as grounds for UNDERDETERMINED, the judge does what K-S2 forbids; the verse is not open and both senses stand."}
